events.title: The Critical Balance: Prompt vs. Context Window
events.subtitle: AI-Native Software Development — Only Builders Club
events.speaker: Vahid Faraji
events.description: Vahid breaks down the critical factors that determine the efficiency of AI assistants — context window vs. prompt distinction, token economics, cost management, and IDE planning with GitHub Copilot.
topics: Context Window vs. Prompt — the difference and token economics
Limits, cost management, and IDE planning (GitHub Copilot example)
Spec preparation, refactoring workflows with Numpy/Pandas code examples
takeaways: Understand the distinction between prompt and context window
Learn token economy fundamentals for cost-efficient AI usage
Practical spec preparation techniques for AI-assisted development
Refactoring strategies using real Numpy/Pandas code

events.title: Agent Sessions Day
events.subtitle: VS Code 1.109 — Multi-Agent Development in VS Code
events.speaker: VS Code Team
events.description: Live demos of VS Code 1.109's evolution into a unified agent UX. Covers multi-agent sessions across local, background, and cloud environments, Claude Agent compatibility, agent hooks, message steering and queueing, agent skills as slash commands, terminal sandboxing, and Copilot Memory.
topics: Unified agent UX — local, background, and cloud sessions
Claude Agent SDK integration and Claude file compatibility
Agent Skills (GA) — reusable domain expertise as slash commands
Copilot Memory for cross-session context persistence
Agent orchestration with subagents and parallel execution
takeaways: Understand VS Code's multi-agent session management model
Learn how agent hooks enforce deterministic workflows
Explore context efficiency through subagent isolation
Discover how agent skills package domain expertise
See how terminal sandboxing improves agent security
